day_shape: 105 items: US-Iran post-war diplomacy dominates with Rubio touring Gulf and E4 leaders' statement on the peace deal, Strait of Hormuz contested between IRGC Navy and Oman-Iran talks, IDF reservist killed in southern Lebanon accident, heavy IRIB/Defa Press Ashura cycle.

threads.label: US-Iran peace deal diplomacy
threads.summary: Secretary Rubio toured Kuwait and is closing his trip in Bahrain seeking Gulf support for the US-Iran deal, and spoke with German FM Wadephul on the talks and Hormuz navigation. The UK published a Joint E4 Leaders' Statement on the 14 June US-Iran peace deal, while the US Senate rejected a motion to curb Trump's Iran war powers.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz contested governance
threads.summary: The IRGC Navy stated that safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz is only possible through routes declared by Iran, rejecting a newly announced route issued without Tehran's coordination. Oman and Iran agreed to pursue talks on future administration of the Strait, asserting sovereign rights, while Tanker Trackers reported Iran exported 40 million barrels of crude since 15 June.

threads.label: Iran internal politics and economy
threads.summary: Iran International reported hardline lawmakers escalating opposition to Speaker Ghalibaf over the US agreement, and described Pezeshkian's blunt remarks on the economic crisis intensifying infighting around Mojtaba Khamenei's stance. Defa Press carried a Pezeshkian Ashura post on standing against injustice; Iran International also reported an IRGC lodging complex in Shiraz was a likely target of an early-war strike that killed nine civilians.

threads.label: Southern Lebanon incidents and talks
threads.summary: The IDF announced the death of reservist Master Sgt. Basil Sweid, 32, when his refuelling truck overturned near Rab al-Thalathine, and confirmed an airstrike on a vehicle that crossed the ceasefire line in the Ali Taher ridge. Israeli-Lebanese delegations in Washington discussed a pilot Lebanese Army deployment tied to IDF withdrawals, while Hezbollah's Naim Qassem demanded Israel leave southern Lebanon.

threads.label: Gaza operations and humanitarian moves
threads.summary: The IDF reported a Defense Ministry civilian contractor, Raad Abu al-Qi'an from Hura, was killed in a building collapse during demolition works in Gaza, and announced the killing of Hamas operative Akram Abu Mazi in a Sunday airstrike. The UK Foreign Secretary announced child medical evacuations and university places for Palestinians, while Israeli contractors entered talks on large-scale Gaza rubble removal.

threads.label: Post-war US military fallout
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post reported CBS findings that US soldiers wounded in the Iran war described injuries as more severe than Defense Secretary Hegseth previously stated, and that Trump is set to meet Lockheed, RTX and Boeing on rebuilding missile stockpiles. Trump said he was disappointed with NATO's participation in the Iran war as Secretary General Rutte said European allies supported the US effort.

threads.label: Ashura messaging and Lufthansa claim
threads.summary: IRIB and Defa Press ran a heavy Ashura cycle including processions in Tehran, Kerman, Yazd, Kashan and Khorramabad, and said President Pezeshkian attended mourners in Tabriz. Defa Press and IRIB claimed Lufthansa flights to Iran would resume soon, a claim Lufthansa Group rebutted to Iran International, saying flights remain suspended until 24 October.
